correctness.rationale: The scaled order-polytope facets are explicit. Minimal and maximal boundary normals have norm one; a cover normal is \(s_j e_i-s_i e_j\), so its normalized Euclidean slack yields exactly the edge weight \(\sqrt{s_i^{-2}+s_j^{-2}}\). Summing the radius constraints along any augmented Hasse path telescopes to \(1\ge rL\), giving the upper bound. Longest-prefix and longest-suffix dynamic programs construct feasible centers at \(r=1/L\), proving sharpness. The same path sums sandwich every optimal-center coordinate and give the stated iff uniqueness criterion.

value.rationale: Lecture-hall order polytopes are a natural lattice-polytope family that simultaneously generalizes order polytopes and lecture-hall simplices. Unequal lecture-hall scaling changes Euclidean geometry nonuniformly, so the ordinary height formula does not transfer by affine invariance. The theorem replaces height by a canonical weighted critical-path invariant, provides the complete optimal-center polytope, gives an exact uniqueness criterion, and yields a closed formula for every lecture-hall simplex. The radius and extremal centers are computable in linear DAG time once the Hasse diagram is known. This is a motivated family-wide weighted extension, not an arbitrary parameter slice or finite recomputation.
